events.title: Vitthalpant takes sannyasa, returns, and the family is outcast
events.summary: Father left for Kashi, took sannyasa as Chaitanyashram, was told by his guru to return to householder life, and was then excommunicated by Brahmins. After about twelve years he left the family for penance.
events.date_or_period: before the births of the children
events.narrated_in: Namdev's accounts, Udhavachidghan's Dnyaneshwar Charitra and Bopdev's Shuddhipatra (as named by the entry)
events.earliest_source_status: Earliest narration not identified; the entry cites Namdev's writings first. Poem numbers for the Adi cycle not located

events.title: The parents' end
events.summary: English Wikipedia reports the parents drowned themselves in the Indrayani, with other versions placing Vitthalpant's end in the Ganges; the Vishwakosh has him leave for penance and says nothing of drowning in the extraction.
events.narrated_in: Bahirat 2006 and Glushkova 2014 per English Wikipedia
events.earliest_source_status: Secondary report; not read in the original sources

events.title: Nivruttinath meets Gahininath
events.summary: While the family fled a tiger near Nashik, Nivruttinath hid in a cave and was initiated by Gahininath; he later initiated Dnyaneshwar.
events.narrated_in: Bahirat 2006 and Ranade 1933 per English Wikipedia

events.title: Journey to Paithan and the shuddhipatra
events.summary: The children went to Paithan, where the Brahmin assembly gave a certificate declaring the parents' status and prescribing devotion in place of penance.
events.people_involved: Dnyaneshwar; Nivruttinath; Sopan; Muktabai; Paithan Brahmins
events.narrated_in: Namdev poem 352 mentions the Paithan debate; Gatha Panchak intro describes the shuddhipatra
events.earliest_source_status: Earliest source: Namdev poem (authorship disputed); Britannica also reports the certificate

events.title: The buffalo recites the Veda
events.summary: A buffalo (named Dnyana in Namdev's account per the entry) is made to speak Vedic words, convincing the Paithan scholars. Mahipati's retelling has Dnyaneshwar object to a man beating a buffalo, then touch its head.
events.narrated_in: Namdev poem 352 ("म्हैसीपुत्र" at the debate); Mahipati per Dallmayr
events.earliest_source_status: Namdev poem is the earliest source I could read; its dating is disputed

events.title: The buffalo's end
events.summary: The buffalo is said to have died in a forest on the way to Alandi and to have a samadhi.
events.narrated_in: Entry, citing no text by name

events.title: Sachchidanand revived; scribe of the commentary
events.summary: A dead man, Sachchidanand, a Nevasa Kulkarni, is revived and takes down the Dnyaneshwari. The colophon names him as scribe.
events.narrated_in: Dnyaneshwari colophon names the scribe; the revival is from Namdev's account per the entry
events.earliest_source_status: Colophon (text) gives the scribe; the revival is hagiographic

events.title: Composition of the Dnyaneshwari (Bhavarthadipika)
events.summary: Commentary on the Gita in Marathi ovi, said in tradition to be composed at Nevasa and written down by Sachchidanand; the closing verses give Shaka 1212 and name Nivruttinath's servant Dnyandev. Place: the Vishwakosh says Nevasa; the received text I read names Godavari bank, Mahalaya and king Ramachandra, not Nevasa.
events.earliest_source_status: The text itself is the earliest witness; place name not in it

events.title: Pasaydan (closing prayer)
events.summary: In the closing prayer the deity addressed as Vishwesvarao grants the boon and the poet is pleased (line DNY18_1881).

events.title: Composition of the Amritanubhava
events.summary: Written after the Gita commentary at Nivruttinath's command, about 800 ovis.

events.title: Changdev Pasashti and the moving wall
events.summary: Changdev, an old yogi, came on a tiger after sending a blank letter. Dnyaneshwar replied in sixty-five ovis; the siblings sat on a wall that moved forward, and Changdev yielded and took initiation from Muktabai.
events.narrated_in: Pasashti text (reply) in package; the wall and tiger from Mahipati as cited by the entry
events.earliest_source_status: Wall and tiger not in the Pasashti text; earliest narrator not identified. Mahipati is 1762-1774

events.title: Visoba Chati and the baked bread
events.summary: A Brahmin of Alandi, Visoba Chati, made the potters refuse vessels. When Nivruttinath wanted bread, Dnyaneshwar heated his back and Muktabai baked it. Visoba repented and was called Khechar; he later became Namdev's guru.
events.narrated_in: Entry; earliest source not named in it

events.title: Meeting of Dnyaneshwar and Namdev at Pandharpur
events.summary: The group went to Pandharpur to meet Namdev; Vitthal gave leave. Namdev poems describe Dnyandev coming, Namdev bowing, and a conversation before Vitthal.
events.narrated_in: Namdev poems 202-213 in the e-Sahitya witness

events.title: Pilgrimage with Namdev
events.summary: Companions went with Namdev to Karad (a king's son revived), Marwar (water by Namdev's prayer), Prabhas, Dwarka, Girnar, Ayodhya, Prayag, Kashi and Gaya.
events.people_involved: Dnyaneshwar; Namdev; Chokhamela; Sanvata Mali; Narahari Sonar; Parisa Bhagwat; Visoba Khechar
events.narrated_in: Namdev Tirthavali (1581 solo-journey and 1731 versions differ per the Namdev package record NM2B-EVE008)
events.earliest_source_status: Poems of the Tirthavali not located in the witness; Namdev package record not re-opened

events.title: Sanjivan samadhi at Alandi
events.summary: After a vigil on Ekadashi and a feast on Dvadashi, he entered a pit beside the Siddheshwar temple on Trayodashi; Namdev poems describe Vitthal granting the samadhi and the saints present.
events.narrated_in: Namdev samadhi poems 353-364 in the e-Sahitya witness
events.earliest_source_status: Oldest manuscript of the Samadhi section is dated 1581 (McLaughlin); poem numbers are the witness's own

events.title: Namdev prays and Dnyaneshwar is brought back
events.summary: Story that Namdev prayed to Vitthal and Dnyaneshwar returned for a time.

events.title: Siblings follow within a year
events.summary: Sopandev, Muktabai and Nivruttinath died within a year of his samadhi.

events.title: Eknath's revision of the text, Shaka 1506
events.summary: Eknath, signing as Eka-Janardana, says the Dnyaneshwari was already pure in its origin but corrupted by variant readings and he made a corrected copy, finished at Paithan in Bhadrapad.
events.earliest_source_status: Colophon in the text; scholarly view: see disputes

events.title: Eknath at the samadhi: the tree root and the text
events.summary: Eknath dreams that Dnyaneshwar is choking, goes to overgrown Alandi, finds the cave, removes a root wound around the saint's neck and takes a copy of the Dnyaneshwari from his feet; the tree is called the ajana tree.
events.narrated_in: Eknath Charitra 16.69-77; Bhaktalilamrita 19.120-129 (as cited by McLaughlin)
events.earliest_source_status: McLaughlin does not name the earliest source; Bhaktalilamrita is 1774 per Mahipati page

disputes.question: Birth year
disputes.proponents: Ranade 1933 (as cited); Marathi Wikipedia; Vishwakosh lists it
disputes.current_view_if_stated: English Wikipedia calls it the more accepted tradition

disputes.question: Birth year
disputes.proponents: Pradhan-Lambert 1987 and Ranade pp.31-32 as cited in English Wikipedia; Vishwakosh lists it
disputes.current_view_if_stated: Entry presents both years without choosing

disputes.question: Birthplace
disputes.position: Apegaon (Paithan taluka) as family home and place of birth
disputes.current_view_if_stated: Vishwakosh says the received text does not name his birthplace

disputes.question: Birthplace
disputes.proponents: Britannica; "some scholars" for the siblings in Marathi Wikipedia

disputes.question: Same person or two Dnyandevs
disputes.position: Dnyaneshwari, Amritanubhava and Pasashti are by one Dnyandev, and the simpler abhangas by a later poet of the same name
disputes.proponents: Unnamed scholars in Vishwakosh; McLaughlin reports the argument

disputes.question: Authorship of the abhanga gatha
disputes.position: Many abhangas are probably not his; yoga-theme abhangas, gaulan, virani and Haripath linked to his style; some interpolated

disputes.question: Attributed minor works
disputes.position: About twenty-five works credited to him, including Uttargeeta, Prakritageeta, Panchikaran, Shukashtak, Yogavasistha, are not his by internal evidence

disputes.question: Dating verse of the Dnyaneshwari
disputes.proponents: Doderet 1927 (uses 1290 on its basis); English Wikipedia says the date is undisputed
disputes.current_view_if_stated: Kiehnle argues the verse was added by Eknath in the 16th century (as reported by McLaughlin)

disputes.question: Dating verse of the Dnyaneshwari
disputes.position: The verse was added by Eknath in the 16th century; the text still falls within the reign of Ramachandra (1271-1309)

disputes.question: Place of composition
disputes.evidence_against: S084: closing verses name the Godavari bank and Mahalaya, not Nevasa (my reading of the package text; the Vishwakosh summary says the text itself names Nevasa)
disputes.current_view_if_stated: Flat contradiction between the Vishwakosh summary and the package text; Mahalaya/Nevasa identification not checked

disputes.question: Textual history and Eknath's recension
disputes.position: Interpolation and variants crept in; Eknath prepared a corrected copy in 1584 and no reliable earlier manuscript is known
disputes.evidence_against: DNYL-S02: a Marathi Manuscript Centre record labels one manuscript Shaka 1212 and says the lack of Eknath verses at the end points to great age (cataloguer's view; the date is the catalogue's label)

disputes.question: Eknath recension
disputes.position: Eknath only corrected an already pure text (his own closing verses)

disputes.question: Reliability of Namdev's biographical cycles
disputes.position: Adi, Tirthavali and Samadhi are by the contemporary Namdev and are the main source
disputes.evidence_against: S025: many scholars hold that Namdev could not have overlapped with Dnyaneshwar; oldest Samadhi manuscript is dated 1581
disputes.current_view_if_stated: Britannica: Namdev poems give the oldest account

disputes.question: Vitthalpant's Kashi guru
disputes.current_view_if_stated: Flat contradiction between the two encyclopedias on what Namdev says

disputes.question: Samadhi Shaka year and weekday
disputes.position: Shaka 1218 (Vishwakosh; Marathi Wikipedia body), Shaka 1217 (Marathi Wikipedia infobox); Thursday vs Sunday
disputes.current_view_if_stated: No source checked against an almanac; astronomy test pending

disputes.question: Historicity of miracles
disputes.position: Buffalo, wall and revival stories are hagiography; the Paithan episode shows siblings persuading scholars by conduct and teaching

iconography.note: Scene described in the entry; no picture seen. Not an established icon in the sources read

reception.summary: Poem 352 praises Dnyandev: Changdev bows, the Paithan debate where a buffalo speaks, and the Gita rendered in Marathi; Namdev advises a pilgrimage to Alandi.
Poem 356: Vitthal tells Dnyandev that daily bathing in the Indrayani and the Bhagirathi confluence at Alandi gives Vaikuntha; one who worships at Siddheshvara is dear to him.
Poem 254 lists Nivritti, Dnyaneshwar, Sopan and other saints invited by Vitthal; poem 459 places Dnyaneshwar among a gathering with Vitthal and Rukmai.
Closing verses record that Eknath corrected the text in Shaka 1506 and call the Dnyaneshwari pure; the Alandi legend has him cleaning the samadhi site.
Amritanubhava's influence seen in Eknath's Hastamalak and Swatmasukh; Tukaram's works take up his refutation of Mayavada.
Main early narrative of the life; date and authorship disputed; oldest Samadhi manuscript 1581; some hold Namdev cannot have overlapped with him.

Bhaktavijaya (1762) retells Varkari saint lives including Namdev and Jnaneshwar; Bhaktalilamrita (1774) continues. The Vishwakosh cites Mahipati for the Changdev meeting and English Wikipedia (via Dallmayr) for the buffalo story.

reception.summary: Bhaktavijaya in English by Justin E. Abbott, 1933; Motilal Banarsidass editions 1988 and 1995 (Abbott with Godbole).
Dnyaneshwar Charitra and Shuddhipatra named in the Vishwakosh as sources for the life.
English account of the life and teaching, cited widely for 1275-1296.
Biography and philosophical study; "Jnaneshwar" in Cultural Leaders of India (1978), ed. V. Raghavan.

reception.who: S. V. Dandekar; J. F. Edwards

reception.summary: Grammar of the Jnanesvari (BSOAS 1927) dates the text to 1290 and treats it as a witness of late 13th-century Marathi.
Argues the dating verse is a 16th-century addition by Eknath (as reported).
Two-Dnyandevs question unresolved; abhanga authenticity doubtful; about 25 minor works not his.
Studies the samadhi shrine at Alandi as temple and tomb, the Eknath tree tale, the silver bust and padukas.

Shrine treats the entombed body as a living image with daily waking, bathing, feeding and evening rites; silver padukas go to Pandharpur in the Ashadh pilgrimage, documented since at least early 17th century.
Namdev poems give the oldest account; family treated as outcaste and obtained a purity certificate at Paithan.
